# core:jwt

JSON Web Tokens (RFC 7519) in the JWS Compact Serialization (RFC 7515),
with HMAC-SHA256 (`HS256`, RFC 7518 §3.2) built in.

The key decides the algorithm, never the token. [`verify`] takes a key that
implements [`JwsVerifier`] and checks the signature with _that_ algorithm,
so a header naming another one cannot redirect verification — the
algorithm-confusion class. `alg` is still read, and a token whose header
disagrees with the key is rejected.

An RSA or ECDSA key type defined elsewhere implements the same traits and
works with the same entry points, with no change here to admit it.

Claims stay bytes: [`verify`] returns the payload for the caller to
deserialize with `core:json`, into its own struct or into
[`RegisteredClaims`]. [`RegisteredClaims::validate_time`] checks `exp` and
`nbf` against a time it is passed, so verifying needs no clock effect.

## Synopsis

```wado
let key = Hs256Key::new(&"a 32-byte-or-longer shared secret");
let token = sign(&`{"sub":"joe","exp":1300819380}`, &key);

// Verification hands back the payload bytes; claims are yours to read.
let Ok(payload) = verify(&token, &key) else {
    panic("the token this key just signed must verify");
};
let Ok(claims) = from_bytes::<RegisteredClaims, ByteList>(payload) else {
    panic("the payload is JSON");
};
assert claims.sub == Option::Some("joe");
assert claims.validate_time(1300819379) matches { Ok(_) };
assert claims.validate_time(1300819380) matches { Err(JwtError::Expired) };
```

## Functions

### `pub fn sign<K: JwsSigner, P: AsByteSlice>(payload: &P, key: &K) -> String`

Sign `payload` into a compact JWS: `base64url(header).base64url(payload).base64url(signature)`.

### `pub fn verify<K: JwsVerifier>(token: &String, key: &K) -> Result<ByteList, JwtError>`

Verify `token` with `key` and return its payload bytes.

Checks, in order: three canonical base64url segments, the key's signature
over `header.payload`, the header's `alg` against the key's, and that no
extension is marked critical. Claims are not read: checking `exp` is
[`RegisteredClaims::validate_time`]'s job, and the caller's to invoke.

## Traits

### `pub trait JwsAlgorithm`

The `alg` a key speaks for. Both halves inherit it, so a key that signs
and verifies answers once.

#### `fn alg(&self) -> String`

The `alg` header value, e.g. `"HS256"`.

### `pub trait JwsVerifier: JwsAlgorithm`

The verifying half of a JWS algorithm. Implement it on a key type to teach
[`verify`] an algorithm this module does not carry.

#### `fn verify(&self, signing_input: &ByteList, signature: &ByteList) -> bool`

Whether `signature` is this key's over `signing_input` (the token's
`header.payload` ASCII bytes). An implementation compares with
`eq_constant_time`, never `==`.

### `pub trait JwsSigner: JwsAlgorithm`

The signing half of a JWS algorithm.

#### `fn sign(&self, signing_input: &ByteList) -> ByteList`

## Structs

### `pub struct RegisteredClaims`

The registered claims (RFC 7519 §4.1) this module knows how to check.
`aud` is absent: it is a string _or_ an array of strings on the wire, so it
belongs to a caller's own claims struct until this module carries both.

#### `iss: Option<String>`

#### `sub: Option<String>`

#### `exp: Option<i64>`

#### `nbf: Option<i64>`

#### `iat: Option<i64>`

#### `pub fn validate_time(&self, now: i64, leeway: i64 = 0) -> Result<(), JwtError>`

Check `exp` and `nbf` against `now` (seconds since the Unix epoch),
tolerating `leeway` seconds of clock skew on either side. An absent
claim is not checked. `leeway` widens the window, so it is never
negative.

The time is an argument rather than a clock read, so verifying a token
gains no `SystemClock` effect. Pass `Instant::now().seconds` where you
do have one.

### `pub struct Hs256Key`

A shared secret for `HS256`, signing and verifying with HMAC-SHA256.

_Fields are private._

#### `pub fn new<S: AsByteSlice>(secret: &S) -> Hs256Key`

RFC 7518 §3.2 requires a key at least as long as the hash output. A
shorter secret is brute-forcible, so it is refused rather than accepted.

#### `impl JwsAlgorithm for Hs256Key`

##### `fn alg(&self) -> String`

#### `impl JwsSigner for Hs256Key`

##### `fn sign(&self, signing_input: &ByteList) -> ByteList`

#### `impl JwsVerifier for Hs256Key`

## Enums

### `pub enum JwtError`

Why a token was rejected.

#### `Malformed`

Not three `.`-separated segments, or a segment that is not canonical
base64url, or a header that is not JSON.

#### `AlgMismatch`

The header's `alg` is not the one the key verifies.

#### `CriticalHeader`

The header carries `crit`, which names extensions a recipient must
implement. RFC 7515 §4.1.11 requires rejecting the ones it does not,
and this module implements none.

#### `InvalidSignature`

The signature is not this key's over this token.

#### `Expired`

`exp` has passed.

#### `NotYetValid`

`nbf` has not arrived.
